newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks 60 mln Ecu EIB loan for airport.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks 60 mln Ecu EIB loan for airport.

text.p: Bulgaria will start negotiations on a loan worth 60 million Ecu from the European Investment Bank (EIB) for the reconstruction of Sofia airport, Transport Minister Wilhelm Kraus said on Thursday.

Kraus said the EIB had proposed in a letter on Wednesday to start negotiations based on a feasibility study for modernising the 56-year-old airport worked out by British consulting firm Gibb Business Consulting.

"I think it is realistic that if we sign an agreement with the EIB in July and if the bank's board approves it by the end of the month then in September it could be possible to start using the credit," Kraus told reporters.
He said the first stage of the reconstruction, which includes enlargement of a passenger terminal to handle 3.5 million passengers per year and lengthening the runway, would cost some $120 million.
Another $20-25 million will be needed for a cargo terminal to handle up to 60,000 tonnes per year.
Kraus said Japan could also make a loan for the project. "It could be also Kuwait, Germany's Siemens AG or Deutsche Bank," Kraus said. "We are seeking sources for financing and investment."

President Petar Stoyanov said last month after a visit to Kuwait the Kuwaiti Development Fund had agreed to lend an initial $40 million for the project, with the possibility of more credits later. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
